summary: Yingshan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who was attested as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies in 1996 and retired as an honorary research fellow on February 18, 2023.

Yinke Chen (1890–1969) was a historian, sinologist, and linguist who studied at institutions including Berlin, Harvard, and Zurich, and under Lanman, Lüders, Müller, and Haenisch. He held posts at Tsinghua, Peking University, Academia Sinica, and Sun Yat-sen University.

Yinshun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and Qingnian, and at Taisho University and Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes. He taught at Minnan and Wuchang, served as Fawang Buddhist Institute's head, and led the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

Yirmiyahu Yovel (1935–2018) was a scholar in the field of philosophy. He completed his education at the Hebrew Reali School, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1960–1968), and Princeton University (~1966–1968).
Yiu Wing Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Hong Kong by 2013, studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann (1937–2023) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv, Hanazono, and Kyoto University (PhD ~1972–1977) under Sojo Hirano and Ben-Ami Scharfstein, and was a professor at the University of Haifa (~1975–2003).
Yohei Furukawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Ryuji Hayashi. By 2026, he was attested as an associate professor at Soka University.

Yohei Kawashiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013) and as a special research fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).
Yoichi Fukuda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003 and 2015).
Yong Hua is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College by 2014, studying under MA supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche (born 1975) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sherab Ling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenchen Kunga Wangchuk, becoming abbot of Sherab Ling Monastery (~1998).
Yongshan He is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at McMaster University under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Tsinghua and Harvard under Lanman and Babbitt, he held posts at Southeast, Nankai, and National Southwestern Associated Universities, and served as vice-president of Peking University.

Yongyu Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cornell University and Harvard University. She served as a professor at Joong-Ang Sangha University (attested 2015) and was an ArtTable Fellow at the Public Art Fund in 2025.
Yonten Gonpo was a scholar who studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje. He was a teacher of Dodrupchen Rinpoche and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

Yoshiaki Shimizu (1936–2021) was a scholar in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Harvard University (~1968–1975), he held posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1975–1984) and Princeton University (~1984–2009).

Yoshifumi Honjo (born 1951) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Kyoto University, he served as a professor at Kobe Women's University (2000–2004), Bukkyo University (2014), and Otani University (2010), and as head priest at Anshin-in (2006).

Yoshifumi Mizuno (born 1958) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, Toyo Bunko, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu (1943–2014) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata and Shoson Miyamoto. He served as a lecturer (1971) and professor (2001) at Komazawa University and conducted overseas research at Virginia (1985).

Yoshihiko Amino (1929–2004) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950) and later held posts at Nagoya University (~1967–1980) and Kanagawa University (~1980–1995).
